Package frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve

Class SwerveUtils

java.lang.Object
frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.SwerveUtils
public class SwerveUtils extends Object
Stateless math helpers for swerve module optimization and acceleration-limited velocity stepping.

    • optimizeModuleState

      public static edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.SwerveModuleState optimizeModuleState(edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.SwerveModuleState desiredState, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d currentAngle)
      Optimizes a module's desired state so it never has to rotate more than 90° from its current angle, flipping the wheel direction (and negating speed) instead when that's shorter.
      Parameters:
      desiredState - the target module state
      currentAngle - the module's current steer angle
      Returns:
      an equivalent state reachable via the shortest rotation from currentAngle

    • limitForwardAcceleration

      public static edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d limitForwardAcceleration(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d currentVelocity, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d desiredVelocity, double maxAcceleration, double maxVelocity)
      Steps currentVelocity one 20ms cycle towards desiredVelocity, capping acceleration in the current direction of travel only (a speed-dependent cap: it tapers to 0 as currentVelocity approaches maxVelocity). Lateral (skid) acceleration is left unbounded; see limitForwardAndSkidAcceleration(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d, double, double, double) to also limit that.
      Parameters:
      currentVelocity - the robot's current field/robot-relative velocity
      desiredVelocity - the requested velocity to move towards
      maxAcceleration - the maximum forward acceleration, in m/s², at zero speed
      maxVelocity - the speed, in m/s, at which the forward acceleration cap reaches 0
      Returns:
      the velocity to command for this cycle

    • limitSkidAcceleration

      public static edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d limitSkidAcceleration(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d currentVelocity, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d desiredVelocity, double maxSkidAcceleration)
      Steps currentVelocity one 20ms cycle towards desiredVelocity, capping the magnitude of the acceleration vector uniformly in every direction (unlike limitForwardAcceleration(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d, double, double), which only limits acceleration along the current heading).
      Parameters:
      currentVelocity - the robot's current field/robot-relative velocity
      desiredVelocity - the requested velocity to move towards
      maxSkidAcceleration - the maximum acceleration magnitude, in m/s²
      Returns:
      the velocity to command for this cycle

    • limitForwardAndSkidAcceleration

      public static edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d limitForwardAndSkidAcceleration(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d currentVelocity, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d desiredVelocity, double maxForwardAcceleration, double maxSkidAcceleration, double maxVelocity)
      Combines limitForwardAcceleration(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d, double, double) and limitSkidAcceleration(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d, double) in one step: caps forward acceleration with a speed-dependent taper, then additionally caps the resulting acceleration magnitude for skid protection. This is the limiter Swerve.drive(frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.SwerveSpeeds) uses every cycle to smooth driver/autonomous input into an achievable velocity.
      Parameters:
      currentVelocity - the robot's current field/robot-relative velocity
      desiredVelocity - the requested velocity to move towards
      maxForwardAcceleration - the maximum forward acceleration, in m/s², at zero speed
      maxSkidAcceleration - the maximum overall acceleration magnitude, in m/s²
      maxVelocity - the speed, in m/s, at which the forward acceleration cap reaches 0
      Returns:
      the velocity to command for this cycle
